question: A 3-week-old newborn is brought to the emergency department by his parents because of 4 episodes of vomiting that occurred that morning. The parents report that the vomit was yellowish-green with no blood in it. The patient was born at 38 weeks' gestation via vaginal delivery and has generally been healthy. He has passed normal stools each day. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears irritable and pale. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 146/min, and blood pressure is 90/55 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft, mildly distended abdomen with no masses or organomegaly. A nasogastric tube is inserted and intravenous fluid resuscitation is initiated. An x-ray shows no gas distal to the duodenum. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Yellowish-green vomit" -> "suggests bile" -> "possible intestinal obstruction" -> "x-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "suggests duodenal obstruction" -> "upper gastrointestinal contrast series to confirm" -> 85%

CHAIN: "3-week-old newborn" -> "bilious vomiting" -> "intestinal obstruction likely" -> "x-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "possible malrotation with volvulus" -> "upper gastrointestinal contrast series to assess" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Bilious vomiting" -> "intestinal obstruction" -> "x-ray findings" -> "no gas distal to duodenum" -> "upper GI series to identify level of obstruction" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Newborn with bilious vomiting" -> "intestinal obstruction suspected" -> "x-ray shows no gas beyond duodenum" -> "upper GI series to evaluate for malrotation" -> 70%
analysis: The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn, along with the x-ray finding of no gas distal to the duodenum, suggests a diagnosis of intestinal obstruction, likely due to malrotation with midgut volvulus. This is a surgical emergency. The most appropriate next step in management is an emergent exploratory laparotomy to address the obstruction and prevent bowel necrosis.
